mcp_server.def: A small program that lets an AI assistant use an outside tool or data source through the Model Context Protocol, an open standard.

model.def: The trained AI system that produces text, images or other output. Products and agents are built on top of models.

agent.def: Software that uses a model to carry out multi-step tasks on its own, often by calling tools.

prompt.def: The instructions or text you give an AI model. A prompt template is a reusable one.

skill.def: A packaged set of instructions and files that teaches an AI assistant to do a specific task.

library.def: Reusable code that developers add to their own software.

dataset.def: A collection of data used to train or test AI models.

product.def: A finished AI app or service that you use directly, without writing code.

article.def: Writing about AI: a guide, tutorial or blog post.

paper.def: A research paper, usually from arXiv.

event.def: A conference, meetup, webinar or hackathon.

course.def: A course or a certification about AI. Its platform is listed under Platforms; tags say whether it gives a certification (a proctored exam) or a certificate of completion, and whether it is self-paced, instructor-led, a live event or an exam only.

other.def: An AI resource that fits none of the other types.

glossary.typeAssigned: Helper2 assigns the type from the source's data, keyword rules or an AI model, so it can be wrong.

license.def: The rules for using, changing and sharing the resource. Always read the license itself before relying on it.

open_source.def: The source code is public under a license that lets others use and modify it. It does not always mean free of charge.

tech_level.def: How much technical skill is needed to get started.

platform.def: Where it runs, for example web, desktop, mobile or command line.

popularity.def: Counts such as stars or downloads reported by one source. They are never combined into a single score.

provenance.def: Where a piece of information came from and when it was retrieved.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.lede: Help people find the right AI resource for their need, and show the proof behind every answer.

sections.title: Why Helper2.ai exists
paragraphs: New AI models, tools, agents, MCP servers and papers appear every day. General search engines mix them with marketing pages and old content, so it is hard to know what is real and current.
Helper2.ai searches only sources about AI, tells you which sources it searched, and shows where every result comes from and when it was checked.

sections.title: What we promise
items: Proof before opinion. The guide only recommends a resource when it can quote a real source that supports the choice.
Honest coverage. We list every source we search and show what each one returned. We do not claim to search the whole web.
No invented facts. We never fill in dates, popularity or other facts that no source stated.
Open by default. The source code is public under the Apache-2.0 license.
Privacy first. In Europe, personalised ads and analytics only if you accept them, and we never sell data.

sections.title: How we mark AI text
items: On the screen, every text written by an AI model has a label next to it: “AI-written” in the guide’s picks bar, on its search terms, on its question back to you, on a name it did not find in our sources, on its reasons in the result list and the preview, and on its comparison, explanation and prompt; “Read by AI” on the requirements it read from your question; “AI summary” and “Extracted by AI” on a description or a value in the result list, the preview and on the resource page; “Translated by AI” on the English translation of a query in another language; and “Steps written by AI” in the setup guide.
On the home page, an example a model drafted and a person checked has a small “AI” mark: “Drafted with AI, checked by a person”.
In the page, the same text carries the HTML attribute data-ai-generated="true", and data-ai-model with the model name when we know it.

In our API, a guide answer has an aiContent object that names the provider, the models and the fields they wrote. Catalog values carry an origin such as AI_SUMMARY or AI_EXTRACTED. A search gives the translation of a query in its own field, translatedQuery.
Quotes, titles and links are never written by AI. They come from the sources.

sections.title: Who is behind it
paragraphs: Helper2.ai is an independent project by Silvio Incalza, a software engineer based in Switzerland. The AI guide runs on NVIDIA Nemotron models served by Nebius Token Factory.

sections.title: What we process and why

items.text: Your searches and guide questions: the text you type, used only to answer you. It is not linked to your account. A source's search results count as fresh for a short time, set per source; we keep the stored copy for up to {{cachedSearches}}, so results can still be shown when a source fails. Guide answers are kept for up to {{cachedGuideAnswers}}. Both are stored under a hash of the question, not its text. When you ask the guide on a results page filtered by category, it also gets the ids of the categories you chose: they come from our fixed list, never from what you type. They are part of that hash and are kept with the cached answer for up to {{cachedGuideAnswers}}, not linked to you or your account. A cached guide answer, with the search queries the guide wrote for it, can be shown to anyone who asks the same or a very similar question. Please do not type personal or secret information.
items.withoutNumbers: Your searches and guide questions: the text you type, used only to answer you. It is not linked to your account. A source's search results count as fresh for a short time, set per source; we keep the stored copy for a limited time, so results can still be shown when a source fails. Guide answers are kept for a limited time too. Both are stored under a hash of the question, not its text. When you ask the guide on a results page filtered by category, it also gets the ids of the categories you chose: they come from our fixed list, never from what you type. They are part of that hash and are kept with the cached answer for the same limited time, not linked to you or your account. A cached guide answer, with the search queries the guide wrote for it, can be shown to anyone who asks the same or a very similar question. Please do not type personal or secret information.

items: Your account, if you sign in with GitHub: your GitHub user ID (a number), your display name and when you last signed in. We ask GitHub only for basic profile access. We never see your GitHub password or your e-mail address.
Your display settings, if you are signed in: whether the radar on Home moves between its sources. Kept with your account until you delete it.

Saved items: if you are signed in, each saved resource (its link, title and type) and when you saved it, stored on our server with your account. If you are not signed in, they stay only in your browser; when you sign in, they move to your account.
Reports you send about a resource: the text you write, linked to your account if you are signed in.
Web search counters: Tavily searches per day and feature, under a keyed hash of your IP address and the date (no address stored; days cannot be linked), or your account ID once account limits are on.

Guide question counters: how many new questions the guide answered for you today, and random ids of the questions we gave back (an answer with no pick, or a question that failed), under a keyed hash of your IP address (for IPv6, its /64 network) that changes every day, so we can apply the daily limit in the Terms. The address itself is not stored.

Your limits for today: when you open the site, we read these two counters under the same daily hash of your IP address, or your account once account limits are on, and send only what is left today (guide questions, and web searches for search and the guide) back to your browser, with the time they reset. Reading them does not count as a use, stores nothing new and does not send your address.
Stored Tavily results, under a keyed hash of the question, not its text.

Guide question fingerprints, only when similar-question reuse is on: a list of numbers (an embedding) computed from your guide question, kept with its cached answer so a later question with the same meaning can get that answer. Not linked to you or your account.

Records of our administrators: when a person who runs Helper2.ai acts in the back office (for example, decides a review item or starts a Scout run), we keep their GitHub user ID, the time, what they did, on what, the result and the note they wrote. When they skip a resource in the enrichment queue, the reason they wrote stays with the resource until it is requeued or we no longer list it. When they decide several review items at once, one batch ID links those records. When they point a relationship between two AI resources at the right resource, or rename its target, the relationship records that a person chose the target (not who: that is in the record above); this stays as long as the relationship. When they fix a proposed resource's title, type or tags before accepting it, the resource's record keeps which of these fields a person changed (not who: that is in the record above); this stays as long as we list the resource. This is about the people who run the site, never about visitors.
Usage totals: how many searches we answer, how many had results from only some sources, and how many found nothing. They are counts only: never the text you typed, your IP address or your account.

Technical data: to limit abuse (rate limits and the number of guide questions per day), we count your requests under a keyed hash of your IP address that changes every day. The address itself is not stored with these counts, and the counts of two days cannot be linked. Only when our counter store is down, your IP address is kept in our server's memory for the length of the limit instead. Our servers and our web gateway also write technical logs, which can include your IP address and the pages you request. The address of a search page contains what you typed: your search words and, when you ask the guide, your question. So these logs can keep your search text next to your IP address. Do not type personal data into the search box. Our servers also record request traces: the timing of each step of a request, linked to its log lines by an ID, without your IP address or your search text. We keep these logs and traces for up to 3 months to keep the service running and secure, then delete them.

Google Analytics: which pages you open (the page path and a fixed page name, never your search words, your guide question or the page title), your device and browser type, your approximate location, which Google derives from your IP address, and when you visit. Google signals and ad personalisation are off. Where the EU, EEA, UK or Swiss rules apply, it runs only if you accept it; elsewhere it can run without asking. You can change your answer at any time in the footer ("Privacy choices" or "Cookie settings").

The ad on search pages, when ads are on: your browser loads it from EthicalAds. EthicalAds receives your IP address, which it uses only to find your country and does not store, your browser type, the address of the page without your search words, and up to three topic words that its script picks from the results on the page, to choose a matching ad. It sets no cookies and builds no profile. There is no ad on pages with a guide answer.

Gifts, if you give through GitHub Sponsors or Stripe: the payment happens on their site, under their privacy policy. We receive what their dashboards show us: your name or user name, the amount, the date and, for Stripe, your e-mail address. We never see your card details.

The ad on resource pages, when ads are on: your browser loads it from Google AdSense. Google receives your IP address, your browser and device data, and the address of the resource page, which never contains your search words. Where the EU, EEA, UK or Swiss rules apply, Google uses cookies and personalised ads only if you accept them in Google's consent question, and otherwise shows limited ads without personalisation. Elsewhere Google can personalise ads under its own policies. There is never a Google ad on a search page or next to a guide answer.

Google's consent question, when Google ads are on: Google's consent tool (Privacy & messaging) asks visitors where the EU, EEA, UK or Swiss rules apply, for Google AdSense and Google Analytics together, and keeps your answer in its cookies. It sees the address of the page, so it does not load on a page with your search words or guide question.

sections.title: Legal basis
items: Answering your searches and guide questions, your account and your saved items: to provide the service you ask for (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).
Rate limits, technical logs, usage totals and the security cookie: our legitimate interest in keeping the service secure and available (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Web search counters, guide question counters and stored results: legitimate interest in a free service at bounded cost (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Reports you send: our legitimate interest in keeping the information on Helper2.ai correct (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

Describing public AI resources with names, titles and short quotes or excerpts from their public pages and from web pages found by our searches: our legitimate interest in showing what a resource is and where each fact comes from (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

Google Analytics and its cookies: your consent where the EU, EEA, UK or Swiss rules apply (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR, and the consent rules for cookies), elsewhere our legitimate interest in knowing how the site is used (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). You can withdraw your consent at any time in the footer; we then stop it and delete its cookies.
The ad on search pages: our legitimate interest in funding a free service (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
Gifts: to handle the gift you chose to make, and our legal duty to keep accounting records (Art. 6(1)(b) and (c) GDPR).
Personalised Google ads and their cookies: your consent, given in Google's consent question. Ads without personalisation: our legitimate interest in funding a free service (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

sections.title: Cookies and browser storage
items: A session cookie, only when you sign in, so you stay signed in.
A security cookie (XSRF-TOKEN) that protects forms against cross-site request forgery.

Browser storage for your light or dark theme, the AI tool you chose in the setup guide and, if you are not signed in, your saved items. When you sign in, the page you were on is kept in this tab until you are back on it, then removed. When a new version of the site is out while a tab is open, the tab keeps the address of the page it reloaded and the time, so it does not reload the same page again right away. The tab also keeps where you had scrolled on each page, so Back returns you there. When you open a result, the tab's history keeps, with that step, the address of your search and, if the guide picked the result, the pick: its rank, its AI-written reason, the quote it checked and the requirements from your question it checked, so the resource page can say why the guide picked it. All of this is gone when you close the tab. This data stays in your browser and is not sent to us, with one exception: when you sign in, the items you saved in this browser are moved to your account and removed from the browser.
Browser storage for your answer to the analytics question (h2.consent), so we do not ask again. It holds only yes or no and the date.

Google Analytics cookies (_ga and _ga_ followed by an ID): they let Google tell that two visits come from the same browser. Where the EU, EEA, UK or Swiss rules apply, only if you accept. They last up to 2 years. If you reject or withdraw your consent, we delete them.
Google's consent tool, when Google ads are on: its cookies (FCCDCF, FCNEC) keep your answer to its question, for up to 13 months.
Google AdSense cookies (such as __gads, __gpi and __eoi), on resource pages: where the EU, EEA, UK or Swiss rules apply, only if you accept them in Google's consent question.
All of these, except the Google Analytics, consent tool and AdSense cookies, are strictly necessary for the site to work. The EthicalAds ad sets no cookies.

sections.title: Who receives data
items: Search sources: to find results, your search text is sent to the sources that answer live, such as GitHub, Hugging Face, npm, arXiv and Tavily. The Sources page lists them all. Each provider handles the request under its own privacy policy, and some of them are in the United States.

Tavily (United States): your search text or the guide's web query, unless a stored result answers. Tavily also receives the addresses of AI products' own web pages, so it can read those pages for us. These addresses are public and contain no data about you.

AI models: guide questions, and searches written in a language other than English, are sent to NVIDIA Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory (Nebius B.V., Netherlands). The model that plans the search and translates runs in the European Union (Finland). The model that chooses the results and checks their reasons runs in the United States, so your guide question and the results it chooses from reach the US. We send only the text, never your IP address or account data.

AI models also read public text about AI resources (source descriptions, web page excerpts, README files, model cards and pages of a product's own website) to describe them, and to draft example searches for the home page, on NVIDIA Nemotron models on Nebius Token Factory in the European Union. It is public text about the resources, not about our visitors. The same public text (a resource's title and description) is also sent to the NVIDIA API catalog in the United States to compute its embedding, so search can find a resource by meaning.

Embeddings: your search text, the searches the guide writes from your question, and your guide question when similar-question reuse is on, are sent to the NVIDIA API catalog (NVIDIA Corporation, United States) to compute their embeddings. We send only the text, never your IP address or account data. Under NVIDIA's terms for this service, NVIDIA may log the text to keep the service secure and prevent abuse, and may use it to improve its products and services, including AI models. NVIDIA is certified under the Data Privacy Framework (see Transfers abroad).
GitHub, when you choose to sign in with it.
Network edge: every request to helper2.ai passes through Cloudflare (United States), which routes traffic to our servers. Cloudflare sees your IP address and the request.

Transfers abroad: GitHub, Cloudflare and NVIDIA are certified under the Swiss-US and EU-US Data Privacy Framework and its UK Extension, so those transfers rely on that certification. Nebius's US calls rely on the standard contractual clauses in its data processing agreement. NVIDIA receives your search text, the searches the guide writes, your guide question when similar-question reuse is on, and public text about resources (see Embeddings above). Hugging Face, npm, arXiv and Tavily are not certified. We send them only your search text (and Tavily also public addresses of product pages), never your IP address or account data, and only because it is needed to give you the results you asked for (Art. 17(1)(b) FADP, Art. 49(1)(b) GDPR).

Google Analytics, Google AdSense and Google's consent tool: Google Ireland Limited and Google LLC (United States). Google keeps the analytics data for 2 months. For AdSense, Google is responsible for the data it collects under its own privacy policy.
EthicalAds, run by Read the Docs, Inc. (United States), when ads are on: the request for the ad on search pages.
Gifts: GitHub, Inc. (United States) for GitHub Sponsors, and Stripe Payments Europe, Limited (Ireland) for card gifts. Each one is responsible for the payment data it collects.

Transfers abroad for these: Google, GitHub and Stripe are certified under the Swiss-US and EU-US Data Privacy Framework, so those transfers rely on that certification. For EthicalAds we send only what loading the ad needs, and no account data.
Hosting: our servers are in Germany (European Union).

sections.title: Public data about AI resources

items.text: To describe the AI resources we list, we read public pages about them, such as GitHub repositories, their README files and Hugging Face model cards. We also run fixed web searches through Tavily to find new AI products, articles that compare them and posts about them: {{categories}} categories of AI tools (such as coding, writing, health and legal tools), each searched once a week, {{categorySearches}} searches in all. Once a week we also search for public LinkedIn pages about AI through Tavily: articles, posts, company pages and events. We never visit LinkedIn ourselves: Tavily finds the pages. These searches contain no data about you.
items.withoutNumbers: To describe the AI resources we list, we read public pages about them, such as GitHub repositories, their README files and Hugging Face model cards. We also run fixed web searches through Tavily to find new AI products, articles that compare them and posts about them: a fixed set of categories of AI tools (such as coding, writing, health and legal tools), each searched once a week. Once a week we also search for public LinkedIn pages about AI through Tavily: articles, posts, company pages and events. We never visit LinkedIn ourselves: Tavily finds the pages. These searches contain no data about you.

items.text: From README files and model cards we keep names of projects, organisations and authors, and short quotes of up to {{quoteChars}} characters, each with its source named and a link to it. We do not keep the rest of their text, and we replace email addresses with "[email]" before anything is quoted.
items.withoutNumbers: From README files and model cards we keep names of projects, organisations and authors, and short quotes, each with its source named and a link to it. We do not keep the rest of their text, and we replace email addresses with "[email]" before anything is quoted.

items: From awesome lists on GitHub (curated lists of AI tools) we also build a search index, so a search can find a tool by the words a list uses around it. We keep only the index (word forms, not the text) and the short section heading the tool sits under, for example "Tools > Vector databases". We do not keep the text of the list. We also read the public awesome lists that these lists link to, up to two steps away and at most 30 more a day. When a list links to a product's own website, we keep the link, the words of the link (the product's name), the list and the section heading, so we can check the product by hand. We do not visit the linked website for this. A product found this way is shown only after we have checked it.

items.text: From web pages found by these searches we keep the page title, its link and the excerpt Tavily takes from the page: up to {{articleExcerptChars}} characters for an article, up to {{productPageExcerptChars}} characters for a product page or a post about a product, which we use as evidence to describe it. We also keep what the search said about the page: which search found it, its rank and relevance score, its publication date, the categories its words fit and the address of its small site icon (we do not load or show the icon). We do not keep the full text of the page, its images or any answer Tavily writes. Articles that compare AI tools are shown in search with their excerpt. A product page or a post about a product is shown only after we have checked it by hand. A title or excerpt can name people, for example an article's author or a product's founder.
items.withoutNumbers: From web pages found by these searches we keep the page title, its link and the excerpt Tavily takes from the page, longer for a product page or a post about a product, which we use as evidence to describe it. We also keep what the search said about the page: which search found it, its rank and relevance score, its publication date, the categories its words fit and the address of its small site icon (we do not load or show the icon). We do not keep the full text of the page, its images or any answer Tavily writes. Articles that compare AI tools are shown in search with their excerpt. A product page or a post about a product is shown only after we have checked it by hand. A title or excerpt can name people, for example an article's author or a product's founder.

items.text: From LinkedIn pages we keep the link, a title without the author's name and an excerpt of up to {{quoteChars}} characters. A LinkedIn page is shown only after we have checked it by hand. The link and the text of a post can still name its author.
items.withoutNumbers: From LinkedIn pages we keep the link, a title without the author's name and a short excerpt. A LinkedIn page is shown only after we have checked it by hand. The link and the text of a post can still name its author.

items.text: When a product's facts (price, platforms, licence) are missing, we read up to {{productPages}} pages of the product's own website through Tavily, such as its home, pricing and download pages. We only read pages on the product's own site. Before an AI model reads the text, we remove hidden text and replace email addresses with "[email]" and phone numbers with "[phone]". We never store the raw page. We keep the cleaned text of the product's public pages (hidden text removed, email addresses and phone numbers replaced) for up to {{pageText}} in our cache, only so we can try again if describing the product fails, then it is deleted. We keep short quotes of up to {{quoteChars}} characters that prove a fact, each with a link to its page. Once a product is described, we keep for {{pageRead}} the page address with a fingerprint (a hash) of its text, so we do not read the same page twice.
items.withoutNumbers: When a product's facts (price, platforms, licence) are missing, we read a few pages of the product's own website through Tavily, such as its home, pricing and download pages. We only read pages on the product's own site. Before an AI model reads the text, we remove hidden text and replace email addresses with "[email]" and phone numbers with "[phone]". We never store the raw page. We keep the cleaned text of the product's public pages (hidden text removed, email addresses and phone numbers replaced) for a short time in our cache, only so we can try again if describing the product fails, then it is deleted. We keep short quotes that prove a fact, each with a link to its page. Once a product is described, we keep for a limited time the page address with a fingerprint (a hash) of its text, so we do not read the same page twice.

items: A fact taken from a product's own page is marked "Self-declared by the vendor": it is what the vendor says about itself. A fact is shown only with a quote that states it; without one it shows as "Not stated".

Some values are not facts but estimates: who a resource is for and its technical level. An AI model estimates them from the public text, and we label them "AI-estimated" on the page and in our API. They can be wrong.

items.text: To search by meaning, we send each resource's title and description to the NVIDIA API catalog (United States) to compute its embedding. When NVIDIA rejects such a request, we log the error message it returns, cut to {{errorLogChars}} characters, so we can see why; it can repeat parts of a resource's public title or description, never your search text (a failed search embedding logs only the status code). These logs are kept up to 3 months (see Retention).
items.withoutNumbers: To search by meaning, we send each resource's title and description to the NVIDIA API catalog (United States) to compute its embedding. When NVIDIA rejects such a request, we log the error message it returns, cut short, so we can see why; it can repeat parts of a resource's public title or description, never your search text (a failed search embedding logs only the status code). These logs are kept up to 3 months (see Retention).

items: This data is about the resources. If a quote, title or excerpt names you, you can object or ask us to remove it: write to us at the address above.

sections.title: How long we keep data

items.text: Cached searches: a source's results count as fresh for a short time, set per source, and the stored copy is kept up to {{cachedSearches}}. Cached guide answers and their question fingerprints: up to {{cachedGuideAnswers}}, deleted by the next daily clean-up.
items.withoutNumbers: Cached searches: a source's results count as fresh for a short time, set per source, and the stored copy is kept for a limited time. Cached guide answers and their question fingerprints: for a limited time, deleted by the next daily clean-up.

items: Technical logs and request traces: up to 3 months. Usage totals: 90 days.

items.text: Web search counters: {{webSearchCounters}}. Rate-limit counters: 1 minute or 1 hour (the length of the limit). Guide questions per day: {{guideQuestionCounters}}. Stored results: {{storedWebResults}}.
items.withoutNumbers: Web search counters and guide questions per day: a few days at most. Rate-limit counters: 1 minute or 1 hour (the length of the limit). Stored results: for a limited time.

items.text: English translations of searches typed in another language: {{translations}}. Search vectors (the numbers we use to search by meaning): {{queryVectors}}. Both are stored under a hash of the search, not its text, and deleted from the database within a day after they expire.
items.withoutNumbers: English translations of searches typed in another language, and search vectors (the numbers we use to search by meaning): for a limited time. Both are stored under a hash of the search, not its text, and deleted from the database within a day after they expire.

items.text: Your account, its display settings and your saved items: until you delete them, or {{inactiveAccounts}} after you last signed in. Then we delete the account, its settings and its saved items.
items.withoutNumbers: Your account, its display settings and your saved items: until you delete them, or a set time after you last signed in. Then we delete the account, its settings and its saved items.

items.text: Reports: {{handledReports}} after they were handled. If your account is deleted, your reports stay without your name until then.
items.withoutNumbers: Reports: a set time after they were handled. If your account is deleted, your reports stay without your name until then.

items.text: Records of our administrators' actions in the back office, with their GitHub user ID and the reason or note they wrote: {{adminRecords}}.
items.withoutNumbers: Records of our administrators' actions in the back office, with their GitHub user ID and the reason or note they wrote: for a set time.

items.text: Runtime spending-limit changes in the back office, with their GitHub user ID and the reason they wrote: {{runtimeSettingChanges}}. The latest change of each limit stays until a newer change replaces it.
items.withoutNumbers: Runtime spending-limit changes in the back office, with their GitHub user ID and the reason they wrote: for a set time. The latest change of each limit stays until a newer change replaces it.

items: The sites our search for new AI resources knows by name (writing sites and directories), with the GitHub user ID of the administrator who added each and the reason they wrote: until an administrator removes the site. The record of the change stays with the other administrator records.

items: Quotes from public pages about AI resources: as long as we keep the source record they were read for, and never longer than we list the resource.

items.text: Pages of a product's own website: the raw page is never stored. Their cleaned text: up to {{pageText}}, to try again. The page address and a fingerprint of its text: {{pageRead}}.
items.withoutNumbers: Pages of a product's own website: the raw page is never stored. Their cleaned text: a short time, to try again. The page address and a fingerprint of its text: for a limited time.

Product pages we accepted from a web search or from an awesome list, with the same: as long as we list the product. LinkedIn company pages and events we accepted: as long as we list them. sections.title: Deleting your account
paragraphs: When you are signed in, select your name at the top of the page, then "Delete my account". We delete your account, its display settings and your saved items at once and sign you out. Reports you sent stay, without your name. Signing in again later creates a new, empty account.
You can also write to the address above and we will delete it for you.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the Swiss Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) and, where it applies, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), you can ask what data we hold about you, and ask us to correct, delete or export it. Write to the address above. You can also complain to the Swiss Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC) or to the data protection authority in your country.

sections.title: The service
items: Helper2.ai is a free search over public sources about the AI ecosystem, with an AI guide that answers questions from those results.
We may change, limit or stop the service, or parts of it, at any time and without notice.

items.text: Live web searches: {{webSearches}}; stored results are free. The AI guide: {{guideQuestions}} new questions a day per IP address; a question whose answer is still stored does not count, and an answer with no pick, or a question that fails, does not count either (up to {{freeAnswers}} a day). After that, the guide shows the top search results without AI picks. Limits reset at 00:00 UTC.
items.withoutNumbers: Live web searches: a daily limit each for search and the guide; stored results are free. The AI guide: a daily limit of new questions per IP address; a question whose answer is still stored does not count, and an answer with no pick, or a question that fails, does not count either (within a daily limit). After that, the guide shows the top search results without AI picks. Limits reset at 00:00 UTC.

items: You can use Helper2.ai without an account. If you sign in, you can delete your account at any time: select your name at the top of the page, then "Delete my account". You can also write to us.

sections.title: No guarantee on results and answers
items: Results come from third-party sources, and guide answers are written by AI models. Both can be wrong, incomplete or out of date.

Values labelled "AI-estimated" (who a resource is for, its technical level) are an AI model's estimate, not a fact a source states. Values labelled "Self-declared by the vendor" are what the vendor says about its own product; we do not check them.
Nothing on Helper2.ai is professional, legal, financial, security or other advice. Check important information at the original source before you rely on it.
The service is provided as it is and as available. We do not promise that it is always available or free of errors.

sections.title: Third-party content and links
items: Helper2.ai links to websites, code, models and tools owned by others. We do not control them and are not responsible for their content, availability, licences or security.
Your use of a linked resource is governed by its owner's terms and licence. Check the licence before you use any code or model.

sections.title: Ads and gifts
items: Search pages can show one ad from EthicalAds and resource pages one ad from Google AdSense, each marked "Sponsored". An ad is never part of the results. Ads never change which results you see or their order, and there is never an ad next to a guide answer.
The guide's answers are written by AI and labelled as such. An ad is never written by our AI and never shown as an answer.

Gifts through GitHub Sponsors or Stripe are voluntary. They give no right to any service, feature or result, and they are not refunded except where the provider's terms or the law say so. A gift to helper2.ai is not a donation to a charity and is not tax-deductible.

sections.title: Acceptable use
items: Do not overload, attack or try to break into the service, and do not try to get around rate limits or other protections.
Do not scrape or copy the service in bulk with automated tools.
Do not use Helper2.ai for anything illegal, and do not send reports that are abusive or deliberately false.
We may block access for anyone who breaks these rules.

sections.title: How we describe resources
items: Some text about a resource is written by an AI model from its sources, and is labelled as such. “AI-written” is text a model wrote, such as the guide's picks and reasons. “AI summary” is a description a model wrote from the resource's own pages. “Extracted by AI” is a fact a model read from a source, shown with a quote of that source.
We find many resources with automatic web searches and in curated lists on GitHub. A list article that compares tools is added without review; a product page is added only after a person checks it.
We do not list tools whose main purpose is illegal or deceptive, such as writing fake reviews or getting around the detection of AI-written content.
If you own a resource and its description is wrong, report it on its page or write to us, and we will correct or remove it.

sections.title: Health and legal tools
items: Helper2.ai lists AI tools for health and for legal work. This is not medical or legal advice.

We do not check whether a health tool is approved as a medical device, whether a legal tool is right for your country or your case, or whether what a tool claims is correct. Claims are the vendor's own, quoted with their source. Ask a qualified professional before you rely on any of these tools.

sections.title: Liability
paragraphs: To the extent the law allows, we exclude all liability for damage that results from using Helper2.ai, from relying on results or guide answers, or from the service being unavailable. This does not limit liability for intent or gross negligence (Art. 100 Swiss Code of Obligations) or any other liability that cannot be excluded by law.

Short quotes from README files and model cards are shown as evidence, with their source named and a link to it. The Helper2.ai name and logo belong to Silvio Incalza. The source code has its own licence, linked in the footer.

how.title: How the guide answers
how.lede: Retrieval first, Nemotron second, a validator last. The model never decides what is true.

body.text: A fast Nemotron model turns your words, in any language, into search terms. A normal search across every source then finds up to {{maxCandidates}} real candidates.
body.withoutNumbers: A fast Nemotron model turns your words, in any language, into search terms. A normal search across every source then finds the real candidates.

body.text: A reasoning model picks at most {{maxPicks}} of those candidates, explains why with a quote, and can adapt a ready-to-use prompt from catalog prompts.
body.withoutNumbers: A reasoning model picks a few of those candidates, explains why with a quote, and can adapt a ready-to-use prompt from catalog prompts.

check.title: A validator checks
check.body: Each pick must be one of the candidates, and its quote must appear word for word in that resource’s text. Rejected suggestions are counted and shown.

notStated.title: Missing means unknown
notStated.body: If no source gave a fact, it says Unknown. Dates, popularity and prices are never filled in.

dates.title: Dates are the source’s own
dates.body: Published and updated come from the source. Otherwise you see when Helper2.ai first saw it.

unchecked.title: Every explanation is labelled
unchecked.body: Code checks the quote word for word. A second model call checks the explanation; the page says if it was checked, removed or not checked.

fallback.title: Search keeps working
fallback.body: If the AI model is unavailable, the guide shows the top real results instead, clearly labelled.
